findings.title: Sticky summary bar is fixed inside a container-type element, so it pins to the editor rather than the viewport
findings.body: `.minis-summary-bar` uses `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0` (global.css ~line 285) but it is rendered as a child of `.minis-editor` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx ~line 914), and this change gives `.minis-editor` `container-type: inline-size`. Per MDN's containing-block rules (quoted in csswg-drafts#10102), an ancestor with any `container-type` other than `normal` is the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants. The bar is therefore positioned against the top of `.minis-editor`, the same place as the header card, and not against the viewport. Scenario: add 8 minis and scroll down until the header card leaves the viewport. IntersectionObserver sets `data-visible=true`, but the bar sits at the top of the editor, which is scrolled away, so the user never sees the summary, the 'Изменить' button or the sticky 'Скачать PDF'. `inset-inline: 0` also sizes the bar to the editor's width instead of the full viewport. This defeats the goal's main sticky-bar requirement.
findings.fix: Render the summary bar outside the element with `container-type` (for example as a sibling of `.minis-editor`, or through a portal to `document.body`), or put `container-type` on an inner wrapper that holds only the header card and workspace. The `@container (width < 40rem)` rules for the bar would then need a media query or their own container.

findings.title: Sticky-bar browser test cannot fail on the bar's real hidden or pinned state
findings.body: The test locates the bar's button with `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. The bar has `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:917), and Playwright role locators exclude aria-hidden subtrees. So `toBeHidden()` on load and after clicking 'Изменить' passes because the locator matches nothing, whatever global.css:293-311 does (`visibility: hidden`, `translateY(-100%)`). After scrolling, `toBeVisible()` only needs a non-empty box and no `visibility: hidden`. It does not check that the bar sits at the top of the viewport. A regression where the base rule stops hiding the bar on load, or the bar is not pinned to the viewport (it renders inside `.minis-editor`, which has `container-type: inline-size`), would still pass. happy-dom never fires IntersectionObserver, so this e2e test is the only place that could catch it. This is a test gap on one page, not a product defect.
findings.fix: Locate the bar through a hook that is not a role (`page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or a data-testid). Assert `data-visible='false'` plus `not.toBeInViewport()` on load and after 'Изменить'. After scrolling and before clicking inside the bar, assert `toBeInViewport()` with the bounding box y near 0.

findings.title: Summary text is truncated on narrow screens, hiding some current settings
findings.body: At about 320 px wide, a long summary (format, margins, style, cut marks, numbering, measured scale) does not fit on one line. The `truncate` class replaces the end with an ellipsis, so while the card is off screen the user cannot read the rest of the current settings in the bar.
findings.fix: Allow the summary text to wrap, or give the user a way to see it in full.

findings.title: Sticky bar's PDF button shows no busy, preparing or error feedback; it is only in the off-screen card
findings.body: The bar's 'Скачать PDF' calls the same `download()` and checks the same `canGenerate` as the card's button. All feedback is rendered only in the settings card: the 'Подготовка PDF…' label, the 'Создаём PDF…' / 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status, `draftError`, and the PDF or object-URL generation error stored in `message`. The bar is used when that card has scrolled out of view, so this feedback is off screen. During generation the bar's button just goes grey with a fixed `aria-label="Скачать PDF"`. If the download fails, or the button is disabled while images are being prepared or because of an invalid margin draft, the user sees nothing download and gets no reason. This goes against docs/DESIGN.md's requirement to design loading and error states.
findings.fix: Mirror the card's state in the bar: use the label `busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, and show a short status or error line (busy, preparing, draftError, download error) in `.minis-summary-content`.

findings.title: 'Изменить' focuses before scrolling, so the smooth scroll and reduced-motion branch have almost no effect
findings.body: The handler calls `firstField?.focus()` without `preventScroll`, then `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start' })`. `focus()` already jumps the page to the field instantly, so the later smooth scroll only animates a small adjustment to `block: 'start'` and the scroll margin. The page scrolls twice. Users who allow motion still get an instant jump, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` lookup barely changes anything.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the single `scrollIntoView` handles both the scroll and the motion preference.

findings.title: Accordion primitive has no consumer after the sidebar was removed
findings.body: This change removed the only import of `@/components/ui/accordion`, which was in `PaperMinisGenerator.tsx`. Nothing else in the repo references the file: no page, component, test or doc. It is now dead code in `src/components/ui/`, and future contributors would take it for a supported, in-use primitive.
findings.fix: Delete `src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`, or state in the PR that it is kept on purpose as a library primitive.

findings.title: Scale popover className draws a double edge and repeats or dead-codes the primitive's styling
findings.body: The scale popover's className adds `border border-border`. The `Popover` primitive (`src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37`) always applies `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, and tailwind-merge keeps both, so the popover gets a 1px border plus a 1px ring just outside it. Neighbouring primitives use one edge each: `select.tsx` uses only a border and `dropdown-menu.tsx` only a ring. The className also includes `minis-scale-popover`, which is defined nowhere. `rounded-lg` and `shadow-md` repeat the primitive's defaults, and `bg-surface-elevated` resolves to the same colour as `bg-popover`. Only the width override changes anything.
findings.fix: Reduce the className to `w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-2rem))] p-4`. If a border is wanted, switch the primitive to `ring-border` so there is only one edge.

findings.title: 'popover closes on Escape and an outside click' test duplicates the test.each above it
findings.body: The parametrised test 'closing the printer scale with $close…' (l.102-178) already closes the popover both by Escape and by an outside pointerdown, then clicks the trigger and calls getByRole on the measurement input. If either way of closing broke, that click would toggle the popover shut and getByRole would throw. The focus-return test (l.180-206) also asserts `open: false` after Escape. The standalone test at l.208-239 therefore fails only when those do, with weaker assertions. CLAUDE.md asks component tests not to overlap.
findings.fix: Delete the standalone test, or fold its open/closed assertions into the test.each and make that test the owner of dismissal.

findings.title: Sticky-bar 'hidden' assertions are satisfied by aria-hidden alone, so a CSS regression that leaves the bar visible over the card goes undetected
findings.body: `edit` is `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. The bar carries `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:916), and Playwright's getByRole excludes aria-hidden subtrees by default (includeHidden: false). So `await expect(edit).toBeHidden()` before scrolling and after clicking 'Изменить' passes merely because the locator resolves to nothing — independent of the CSS that actually hides the bar (`.minis-summary-bar { visibility: hidden; transform: translateY(-100%) }` / `[data-visible='true']` in global.css). If that CSS regresses (rule dropped, selector renamed, specificity change), the fixed bar overlays the top of the page while the card is in view and no test fails; the component tests cannot catch it either since happy-dom never drives the IntersectionObserver. The goal requires the tests to fail if the bar's visibility breaks; only the JS (observer → aria-hidden) half is covered.
findings.fix: Locate the bar by a stable non-role hook (e.g. `page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or a data-testid) and assert visual hiddenness directly — `toHaveAttribute('data-visible','false')` plus `toBeHidden()`/`not.toBeInViewport()` on that element — at the initial and post-'Изменить' checkpoints.

findings.title: Браузерный тест не проверяет закрытие popover и восстановление черновика
findings.body: Тест вводит допустимое значение и нажимает Tab, но не проверяет закрытие через Escape или внешний клик, возврат фокуса и восстановление после недопустимого значения. Поэтому регрессия, при которой в браузере popover не закрывается или после закрытия кнопки PDF остаются заблокированы, не будет обнаружена браузерным тестом. Это покрытие явно требуется для изменения.
findings.fix: Добавить браузерные сценарии закрытия через Escape и внешний клик с недопустимым значением, проверкой фокуса и доступности действий PDF.

findings.title: PDF check would pass if the sticky bar downloaded the wrong document
findings.body: The test only checks the `%PDF-` signature. If the sticky bar's button downloaded some other PDF, such as the scale test sheet, instead of the minis, the check would still pass. It does not confirm the requirement that the bar's button does the same thing as the card's button.
findings.fix: Check the downloaded PDF's content for something that independently identifies the loaded minis, or compare it with the card action's output for the same inputs.

findings.title: The "▾" glyph is plain button text, so it becomes part of the scale trigger's accessible name
findings.body:
The printer scale trigger renders `'Масштаб ▾'` (or `… мм ▾`) as plain text. Its accessible name is therefore "Масштаб ▾", and the tests even query by that name. Screen readers read the decorative glyph aloud, for example as "black down-pointing small triangle".

The rest of the component marks the disclosure chevron as decorative: "Сменить высоту" uses `<ChevronDownIcon aria-hidden="true" />`. This new control breaks that pattern, so a keyboard or screen-reader user hears a symbol name as part of the label.
findings.fix: Replace the text `▾` with `<ChevronDownIcon aria-hidden="true" />`, as "Сменить высоту" does, and update the test queries to `'Масштаб'` / `'Масштаб · 91 мм'`.

findings.title: The 'closes on Escape and an outside click' test repeats the dismissal contract already covered by the test.each above it and the focus-return test
findings.body: I tried to find a change that turns this test red and nothing else. Two candidates: make the popover non-dismissable (`isDismissable={false}`), or disable keyboard dismissal. With either one, the onOpenChange commit never runs. The `closing the printer scale with $close…` test.each then fails on both rows, because `enabledAfterClose` stays `[false,false,false]` and reopening through `triggerName` toggles instead. The focus test also fails on `open: false` after Escape. This test adds no change of its own that would make it fail, and neither test says which one owns dismissal. It is extra suite surface that every later reviewer has to read and keep in sync, with no added protection.
findings.fix: Delete this test, or merge its open/closed assertions into the test.each and name that test as the owner of dismissal.

findings.title: Summary-bar PDF button lacks busy, failure and disabled-reason feedback, which renders only in the off-screen card
findings.body: The bar is visible only while the header card is out of view, yet all feedback for its 'Скачать PDF' action renders inside the card. That covers the busy label 'Подготовка PDF…', the 'Создаём PDF…' and 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status lines, the failure `message` (e.g. from reportPdfFailure) and `draftError`. The bar's label never changes. Concrete cases: (1) with an invalid copy count, or while images are still processing, the bar button turns disabled and the reason appears only in the hidden card. (2) If generation started from the bar fails, the error goes into the hidden card and the button re-enables with nothing visible. The old sidebar was sticky and kept these messages next to its button, so this gap is new.
findings.fix: Mirror the busy label in the bar (`busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, with a matching aria-label). When `message`, `draftError` or `preparing` is set, show a short status line in the bar or point to one with aria-describedby.

findings.title: Scale popover className adds the dead `minis-scale-popover` class and repeats the primitive's defaults
findings.body: The popover's className includes `minis-scale-popover`, which no CSS rule or test references; a repo-wide search finds only this line. So the class implies styling or a test hook that does not exist. The same className also passes `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md` and `bg-surface-elevated` again, which the new Popover primitive already sets (`--color-popover` resolves to surface-elevated). It adds `border border-border` on top of the primitive's `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, so the popover ends up with two outlines.
findings.fix: Remove `minis-scale-popover` and cut the className down to what differs from the primitive (the width and `p-4`). Keep either the border or the ring, not both.

findings.title: Sticky summary bar uses translucent backdrop blur and a drop shadow, which DESIGN.md forbids, and the DESIGN.md edit in the same change never mentions the bar
findings.body: The new `.minis-summary-bar` styles are `background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-surface-elevated) 94%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 1rem oklch(0 0 0 / 8%); backdrop-filter: blur(0.75rem);`. That is a frosted-glass bar with a drop shadow. docs/DESIGN.md:58 forbids glass shadows and glassmorphism, and docs/DESIGN.md:152 rules out drop-shadow by default. This change also edits DESIGN.md (lines 95 and 97) to describe the header card but says nothing about the sticky bar or the scale popover, so the doc and the shipped UI now disagree.
findings.fix: Give the bar an opaque `var(--color-surface-elevated)` background with the existing bottom border, and drop `backdrop-filter` and `box-shadow`. Alternatively, write the bar into DESIGN.md as an explicit exception.

findings.title: Summary-bar hidden assertions pass even when the bar is visibly on screen
findings.body: getByRole skips elements inside aria-hidden="true", and toBeHidden also passes when no element is found. The component sets aria-hidden separately from the CSS, so both hidden checks (lines 298 and 328) pass even if a transform or visibility bug keeps the bar on screen the whole time. The test therefore cannot catch a break in the rule that the bar appears only after the settings card scrolls out of view.
findings.fix: Check that the bar is hidden with a CSS locator that finds it regardless of aria-hidden. For the button, use getByRole with includeHidden: true.

findings.title: Summary-bar PDF button lacks busy/failure/blocked feedback, which renders only in the off-screen card
findings.body:
Observed: the bar's PDF button (lines 946–953) always has the label and aria-label 'Скачать PDF'. All feedback for that action renders only in `.minis-header-pdf` inside the header card (lines 852–866, 872): the busy label 'Подготовка PDF…', the 'Создаём PDF…' and 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status lines, `message` (e.g. the failure text set by `reportPdfFailure`) and `draftError`. The bar is only visible while that card is out of the viewport.

What follows: a user scrolls down to the rows and clicks 'Скачать PDF' in the bar. While the PDF is generated, the button just turns disabled with no label change. If generation fails, the error goes into the hidden card and the button re-enables with nothing visible. If a row draft is invalid or images are still processing, the bar button is disabled and the reason is shown only in the card. The `role="status"` regions still announce to screen readers, but sighted users get no explanation. So the bar's action starts the same operation as the card's button, but it does not behave the same from the user's side, which the goal asks for.
findings.fix: Mirror the busy label in the bar (`{busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'}` plus the matching aria-label). When `message`, `draftError` or `preparing` is set, show a short status in the bar, or make the bar's 'Изменить' path surface it.

findings.title: Тест ищет миниатюру до закрытия модального popover
findings.body: После ввода 97 появляется кнопка «Сбросить измерение». Tab переводит фокус на неё и оставляет popover открытым. Popover использует стандартный модальный режим [React Aria](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Popover#popover), который скрывает внешние элементы от accessibility tree. Поэтому finalMini, заданный через getByRole('article'), не находится: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() завершается по таймауту до проверки панели. Этот новый сценарий блокирует обязательный browser-check даже при исправном интерфейсе. Вывод получен чтением кода; тест не запускался.
findings.fix: После Tab явно закрыть popover через Escape и дождаться его закрытия, затем прокручивать страницу к finalMini.

findings.title: baseStyleSummary is a second copy of the baseStyleOptions labels, lowercased by hand
findings.body: `baseStyleSummary` (lines 71-75) holds the same three labels as `baseStyleOptions` (lines 64-68), just lowercased. If someone renames a label and updates only one table, the header Select and the sticky summary bar will show different names for the same setting. `Record<BaseStyle, string>` checks that every key is present, not that the text matches.
findings.fix: Drop `baseStyleSummary` and derive the text: `baseStyleOptions.find(({ value }) => value === settings.baseStyle)?.label.toLocaleLowerCase('ru-RU')`.

findings.title: The 'closes on Escape and an outside click' test repeats the dismissal checks in the two tests before it
findings.body:
Here is the edit that turns this test red: make the popover non-dismissable, for example `isNonModal`, or stop Escape from closing it. The same edit already fails the two tests just before it:
- The focus-return test (line 179) asserts `open: false` after Escape.
- The `test.each` (lines 104-177) closes the popover by Escape and by outside pointerdown, then clicks the trigger and calls `getByRole('spinbutton')`. If the popover had not closed, that click would toggle it shut and `getByRole` would throw.

So this test catches no defect the others miss. It adds a third place to keep in sync, and nothing says which test owns the dismissal contract.
findings.fix: Either delete this test, or keep it as the single owner of dismissal and make the `test.each` and focus tests assert only the draft commit and focus return.

findings.title: Summary-bar download test would accept the printer test sheet instead of the minis PDF
findings.body: The new sticky-bar test checks the downloaded file only for the `%PDF-` signature. If the bar button's handler were swapped for `downloadPrinterScaleTestSheet()`, the test would still pass: a download happens, the signature matches and the other checks still hold. The user, however, would get the calibration ruler instead of their minis.
findings.fix: Assert `download.suggestedFilename()` against `^paper-minis-\d{8}-\d{4}\.pdf$`, as the existing `uploads a front and back and downloads a PDF` test does.

findings.title: «Изменить» focuses the format trigger before scrolling, so the smooth (reduced-motion-aware) scroll never plays
findings.body: The summary bar's «Изменить» handler calls `firstField?.focus()` with no `preventScroll`, then calls `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto' })`. The header is always off-screen at that moment, because that is the only time the bar is visible. A plain `focus()` scrolls the focused element into view instantly, so the page jumps to the Формат trigger in one step. The smooth `scrollIntoView` then only moves the last few pixels to the card's scroll margin. The `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')` check therefore does nothing: users who allow motion never get the animated return. Final position and focus are correct, and the e2e test checks only those, so it can't catch this.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the explicit `scrollIntoView` controls the motion, or focus after the scroll.

findings.title: The summary bar's PDF button shows no busy label, status or error; all of that feedback stays in the off-screen card
findings.body:
The bar shows only while the header card is out of view. Its `Скачать PDF` button uses the same `disabled={!canGenerate}` and calls the same `download()` as the card's button. But all feedback for that action is rendered inside the off-screen `.minis-header-pdf`: `draftError`, the preparing/busy status («Обрабатываем изображения», «Создаём PDF…»), `message` (set by `store.reportPdfFailure()`) and the busy label «Подготовка PDF…». The bar shows only `settingsSummary` and a fixed «Скачать PDF» label and `aria-label`.

Concrete cases:
(1) While images are still preparing, or while a margin/count draft is invalid, a sighted user sees the bar's button disabled with no reason.
(2) Clicking download in the bar keeps the label «Скачать PDF» and shows no progress, while the card's button switches to «Подготовка PDF…».
(3) If generation fails after a click in the bar, the failure message appears only in the off-screen card.

Live regions do announce to screen readers, but sighted users don't see it. Also, `Изменить` focuses the Format select rather than the field that is actually invalid.
findings.fix: Use the card's label on the bar button (`busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`), and show a short status/error line (`draftError` / busy / preparing / `message`) inside `.minis-summary-content`.

findings.title: The bar-hidden assertion still passes if the bar stays visible
findings.body: If the CSS stops hiding the summary bar while the settings card is visible, the assertions here and at line 328 stay green. The component keeps `aria-hidden=true`, so `getByRole` excludes the «Изменить» button, and `toBeHidden` passes when no element matches. A user would still see a stray fixed bar over the page. So the test has no real guard against a regression in the bar's visibility.
findings.fix: Check visual hiding with `page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')`, which finds the bar regardless of `aria-hidden`, and assert the `aria-hidden` state separately.

findings.title: The bar's PDF button shares the card's enabled state, but the reason it is disabled or failed is shown only in the out-of-view card
findings.body:
Observed: the bar's `Скачать PDF` uses `disabled={!canGenerate}` and calls the same `download()` as the card. All of the feedback for that action stays inside `.minis-header-pdf`, which by definition is out of view whenever the bar shows. That feedback is: `draftError`, the `preparing`/`busy` status, `message` (which `store.reportPdfFailure()` sets) and the busy label `Подготовка PDF…`. The bar renders only `settingsSummary` and a fixed `Скачать PDF` label.

Inferred consequence: a user is scrolled down in the minis list and enters an invalid copy count in a row (`rowDraftError`), or images are still processing. The bar's PDF button goes disabled with no visible reason. Likewise, if generation fails after a click in the bar, the failure message appears only in the off-screen card, so a sighted user sees nothing happen. `Изменить` then focuses the Format select, not the field that is actually invalid.

The goal asks that the bar's actions 'do what the card's do'. The action does, but its feedback is not carried over.
findings.fix: Render `draftError` / the busy and preparing status / `message` (or a short version) inside `.minis-summary-content`, and use the same busy label as the card. Alternatively, make `Изменить` focus the invalid field when `draftError` is set.

findings.title: The scale popover's className has a dead hook class and repeats the primitive's own defaults
findings.body: The `className` passed to `<Popover>` starts with `minis-scale-popover`, and nothing uses that class: there is no rule in `src/styles/global.css` and no selector in src or tests. The string also adds `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md` and `bg-surface-elevated`. The primitive in `src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37` already applies `rounded-lg` and `shadow-md`, and its `bg-popover` resolves to the same colour (`--color-popover: var(--color-surface-elevated)`). So four of the eight classes change nothing in the rendered popover, and they suggest a CSS hook and a style override that don't exist.
findings.fix: Reduce the className to `w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-2rem))] border border-border p-4` and drop `minis-scale-popover`.

findings.title: `baseStyleSummary` hand-copies the `baseStyleOptions` labels in lowercase
findings.body: The new `baseStyleSummary` record ('складная', 'плоская', 'на пенокартоне') is exactly the `label` of each entry in `baseStyleOptions` (lines 65-69) passed through `toLowerCase()`. Lowercasing these Cyrillic strings has no locale quirks, so the output is identical. With two tables, a later wording change to a style label has to be made twice. If only `baseStyleOptions` is edited, the summary bar shows stale wording next to a select that reads differently, and the `Record<BaseStyle,string>` type does not catch that mismatch.
findings.fix: Remove `baseStyleSummary` and build the segment from the existing table: `baseStyleOptions.find(({ value }) => value === settings.baseStyle)?.label.toLowerCase()`. The existing `.filter(Boolean)` already drops `undefined`. Alternatively, hoist the label lookup that `SelectValue` already does and reuse it.

findings.title: Fixed summary bar can cover focused controls in the minis list; no scroll-padding reserves its height
findings.body: `.minis-summary-bar` is `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0; z-index: 40` with `min-block-size: 3rem` plus padding and border. It's visible the whole time the user works in the minis list. Nothing reserves space for it: only the header card gets `scroll-margin-block-start`, and the scroller has no `scroll-padding-block-start`. When a keyboard user Shift+Tabs upward through the row controls (count, height, custom size, delete), the browser scrolls each newly focused control only to the top edge, which puts it under the bar. The focused control is then hidden, which fails WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured). The old layout had no fixed overlay, so this is new with the change.
findings.fix: Reserve the bar's height while it's shown, e.g. `html:has(.minis-summary-bar[data-visible='true']) { scroll-padding-block-start: 4rem; }`, or give the row controls a matching `scroll-margin-block-start`.

findings.title: Settings summary in the bar is truncated to one line on narrow screens
findings.body: The summary uses `truncate` and sits on a single line. On a mobile-width screen, the string with format, margins, base style, trim, numbering and scale doesn't fit, so the last settings disappear behind an ellipsis. There's no other way to expand the summary, so the user can't check those settings in the bar before downloading the PDF.
findings.fix: Let the summary wrap onto several lines on narrow screens, or give another way to see the full text.

findings.title: Summary-bar PDF button gives no visible status; busy, draft-error and failure text render only in the off-screen header card
findings.body: The bar's `Скачать PDF` calls the same `download()` and uses the same `disabled={!canGenerate}` as the card's button. All the feedback for that action is rendered only inside `.minis-header-pdf`: `message` (the failure text set by `reportPdfFailure`), the busy/preparing status and `draftError`. The bar is visible only while that card is out of view. Before this change the settings aside was `position: sticky`, so that text stayed on screen. Failure cases: (1) the user scrolls down, clicks the bar's PDF button, and PDF or object-URL creation fails. The error appears in the off-screen card, so a sighted user sees nothing happen. (2) The user enters an invalid copy count in a row far down. The bar's button goes disabled, but the reason is shown only in the hidden card. Also, the bar's button keeps the fixed label and `aria-label` «Скачать PDF» while `busy`, whereas the card's button switches to «Подготовка PDF…».
findings.fix: Mirror the card in the bar: use `busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'` for its label and aria-label, and show `draftError || message` (or a short status) in `.minis-summary-content`.

findings.title: `Изменить` focuses before scrolling, so the default focus scroll jumps the page and cancels the requested smooth scroll
findings.body: `firstField?.focus()` is called without `{ preventScroll: true }`. By default `focus()` scrolls the element into view immediately. The later `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })` then has almost no distance left to animate. With motion allowed, the user gets an instant jump plus a small adjustment, not the slide the code chooses through `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')`. The `shouldAnimate` branch has almost no effect.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`, or call `scrollIntoView` first and focus with `preventScroll`.

findings.title: Sticky-bar e2e assertions don't pin the bar's real on-screen visibility, so CSS regressions go unnoticed
findings.body: Two gaps mean the test can't tell when the bar's CSS breaks. (1) The 'visible' checks use `toBeVisible()`, which doesn't require the element to be in the viewport, and Playwright scrolls the PDF button into view before clicking it. If `.minis-summary-bar` lost `position: fixed` and rendered in document flow, every assertion would still pass. (2) The 'hidden' checks query `getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`, which skips aria-hidden subtrees. The bar has `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}`, so `toBeHidden()` passes no matter what CSS applies. Removing `visibility: hidden; transform: translateY(-100%)` from the base rule would leave the bar permanently covering the top of the page, and the test would stay green. The goal asks that the browser test fail if the bar's visibility broke.
findings.fix: Query the bar in a way that ignores accessibility state (`page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')`, or `includeHidden: true`). Assert `not.toBeInViewport()`/`toBeHidden()` while the header is in view, and `toBeInViewport()` (or `boundingBox().y` ≈ 0) after scrolling, before clicking its PDF button.

findings.title: «Изменить» focuses the Формат trigger before scrolling, so the smooth scroll and reduced-motion branch have almost no effect
findings.body: The bar's «Изменить» handler calls `firstField?.focus()` without `preventScroll`. While the bar is visible, the header card is above the viewport, so `focus()` instantly scrolls the Формат trigger into view. The later `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start' })` then has only a few pixels left to animate. Users without reduced motion get the same instant jump as users with it, so the `prefers-reduced-motion` check decides almost nothing. Focus still lands correctly, so the impact is limited to the transition.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`, or run `scrollIntoView` first and then focus with `preventScroll: true`.

findings.title: Summary bar's translucent blurred backdrop contradicts DESIGN.md's ban on glassmorphism
findings.body: docs/DESIGN.md:58 says «Без градиентов, теней-стекляшек, glassmorphism», and line 154 says not to use drop-shadow by default. The new `.minis-summary-bar` combines a 94%-opaque `color-mix(... transparent)` background, `backdrop-filter: blur(0.75rem)` and a `box-shadow`, which is the frosted-glass treatment the design doc rules out. The same change edits DESIGN.md but doesn't record this exception and doesn't mention the summary bar at all. A later contributor following the doc would treat the two as in conflict.
findings.fix: Use an opaque `var(--color-surface-elevated)` background with the existing border and no backdrop blur. Otherwise, record the exception for the summary bar in DESIGN.md.

findings.title: Browser test never checks that closing the popover restores an invalid draft or returns focus
findings.body: The browser scenario opens the printer-scale popover, enters a valid value (97) and presses Tab. It never enters an invalid value such as 79 and then closes the popover with Escape or an outside click, so in a real browser it never checks the restored draft, that the PDF actions are enabled again, or that focus returns to the trigger. Component tests do cover all of this in happy-dom (`PaperMinisGenerator.test.tsx:100-206`: Escape and outside pointerdown, restored value, PDF actions, focus return). The gap is limited to browser-only failures, such as a real pointerdown/pointerup click sequence or an overlay catching the outside click. The goal lists browser-test coverage of dismissal and focus return, so the gap is worth closing. The project's own rule, though, is to add browser scenarios only for behaviour happy-dom can't see, so this is a minor coverage gap, not a major one.
findings.fix: Add browser scenarios: enter an invalid value, close with Escape and with an outside click, then assert the restored value, that the PDF actions are enabled, and that focus returns to the trigger on Escape.

findings.title: Кнопка сводки сообщает об ошибке в карточке вне экрана
findings.body: Если создание PDF или создание URL для скачивания завершается ошибкой после нажатия кнопки в сводке, сообщение об ошибке отображается только в карточке настроек. Карточка в этот момент вне экрана, поэтому пользователь не видит причину отсутствия загрузки.
findings.fix: Показать сообщение о результате рядом с кнопкой в сводке или в другом видимом месте.

findings.title: 'Изменить' focuses before scrolling, so the smooth / reduced-motion scroll choice has no visible effect
findings.body: The 'Изменить' handler calls `firstField?.focus()` before `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start' })`. A plain `focus()` scrolls the focused element into view itself. No `scroll-behavior` is set anywhere in src/, so that scroll is instant. Chromium centres the focused element when it has to scroll. So the long jump from the minis list back to the `Формат` trigger happens at once, and the later smooth `scrollIntoView` only moves the remaining distance from about mid-viewport to the card's top edge. Users with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` see an instant jump plus a short glide, not the intended animated return, so the `matchMedia`/`shouldAnimate` branch has almost no effect.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` so that `scrollIntoView` alone does the scrolling.

findings.title: `minis-scale-popover` class has no CSS rule or selector anywhere
findings.body: The scale popover gets `className="minis-scale-popover …"`, but `rg minis-scale-popover` over src/, tests/ and docs/ returns only this line. `global.css` defines every other new `minis-*` class added in this change, but not this one, and no test selects by it. The class does nothing and suggests a style hook that doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Remove `minis-scale-popover` from the className, or add the rule it was meant to carry.

findings.title: Accordion primitive loses its last caller after the sidebar removal
findings.body: PaperMinisGenerator's settings sidebar was the only importer of `@/components/ui/accordion`. After this change, `rg "ui/accordion" src` returns nothing, so the module is dead code in the shared ui folder. The file predates this change, but this change is what leaves it unused. Tailwind v4 scans every non-ignored project file for classes, so the accordion's utility classes are still emitted into client CSS. That matters because this change adds about 3.6 kB to `global.css`, which is under a 10 kB Client CSS limit. A future contributor may also end up maintaining or theming a primitive that nothing renders.
findings.fix: Delete `src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`, or keep it on purpose as part of the shadcn primitive set and say so.

findings.title: Shared Popover's built-in ring stacks with the caller's border (double edge), and most default classes get overridden
findings.body:
The new `Popover` primitive ships the full shadcn class string: `w-72 p-2.5 bg-popover shadow-md ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, plus tw-animate enter/exit/zoom/slide utilities. Its only caller, the scale popover at PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:786, overrides width, padding, background, radius and shadow with `rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-elevated p-4 shadow-md`. That is the same set `SelectContent` uses. `tailwind-merge` treats `ring-*` and `border*` as separate groups and keeps both, so the popover renders a 1px border plus a 1px box-shadow ring outside it.

Neighbouring primitives use only one edge: `DropdownMenuContent` uses `ring-1 ring-border`, `SelectContent` uses `border border-border`. The animation utilities are used by no other ui primitive, so Tailwind emits them only for this popover, and they count against the Client CSS budget.
findings.fix: Give `Popover` the base set `SelectContent` already uses (border border-border bg-surface-elevated rounded-lg shadow-md …) and drop the ring, so the caller only adds width and padding. Or keep the ring as `ring-border` and have callers stop adding a border. Drop the tw-animate utilities unless the motion is wanted.

findings.title: The summary bar's 'Скачать PDF' gives no visible feedback: progress, failure and the reason it is disabled only show in the off-screen card
findings.body:
The goal says the bar's actions must do what the card's do. The click itself does: the bar button calls the same `download()` and uses the same `disabled={!canGenerate}` gate. The feedback around it does not come along. Everything that explains the PDF action lives only in `.minis-header-pdf`:
- the busy status 'Создаём PDF…' and the 'Подготовка PDF…' label,
- `message`, which holds both the success text and the failure text `store.reportPdfFailure` sets,
- `draftError`.

The bar is only visible while that card is out of view (`data-visible={headerOutOfView}`).

How it fails: a user scrolls down a long list of minis and clicks 'Скачать PDF' in the bar.
- If generation fails, the bar looks the same as before. The error only appears in the card above the viewport, so the user gets no PDF and no sign of why.
- If a row's copy count holds an invalid draft, the bar's button is just disabled. The `draftError` text that explains it is off-screen too.

The bar button also keeps `aria-label="Скачать PDF"` while busy, unlike the card button. The fieldset disables it, but it never says the PDF is being prepared.

This was introduced by the change, which added the bar.
findings.fix: Show the busy/failure/draft-error state in the bar too. The smallest version renders `message`/`draftError` (or a short status) next to the bar's buttons. At minimum, mirror the card button's busy label: `aria-label={busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'}` and the matching text.

findings.title: Sticky bar's 'Скачать PDF' gives no visible feedback: busy, failure and draft-error text render only in the off-screen card
findings.body:
The bar's button always reads 'Скачать PDF' and uses the same `download()` and `disabled={!canGenerate}` gate as the card. Everything that explains the action renders only inside `.minis-header-pdf`: the 'Создаём PDF…' busy status, the `message` status (the success text, or the failure text set by `store.reportPdfFailure`), `draftError`, and the card button's 'Подготовка PDF…' label. The bar is visible only while that card is out of view (`data-visible={headerOutOfView}`), so that text is always off-screen while the bar is in use.

Scenario: a user scrolled down to the minis list clicks the bar's PDF button. If generation fails, the bar looks unchanged and the error appears in the card above the viewport, so a sighted user gets no PDF and no explanation. A screen-reader user still hears it through role=status. If a row's count draft is invalid, or images are still preparing, the bar shows a disabled button with no reason given. While busy, the bar button also keeps `aria-label="Скачать PDF"`. Before this change the settings aside was `position: sticky`, so these messages stayed next to the workspace.
findings.fix: Show the busy label on the bar button (`busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, including the aria-label) and render `message`/`draftError` (or a compact status) in the bar. Alternatively, scroll the card into view when either is set.

findings.title: Fixed summary bar has no scroll-padding, so keyboard focus scrolled to the viewport top lands under it
findings.body:
`.minis-summary-bar` is `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0`, with `min-block-size: 3rem` plus padding. It is visible exactly while the user works in the minis list (rendered at PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:911-915). Nothing sets `scroll-padding-block-start` in src/styles, src/layouts or the component. The only scroll offset is `scroll-margin-block-start` on the header card.

Scenario: a keyboard user Shift+Tabs upward through the mini rows (count inputs, height pickers, menu/delete buttons). The browser scrolls each newly focused control only until it reaches the viewport's top edge, which is under the bar, so the focused control is hidden (WCAG 2.4.11, focus not obscured). The control still works.
findings.fix: While the bar is visible, set `scroll-padding-block-start` on the root, e.g. `html:has(.minis-summary-bar[data-visible='true']) { scroll-padding-block-start: 4rem; }`. Or give the minis rows a matching `scroll-margin-block-start`.

findings.title: `minis-scale-popover` class has no rule or selector anywhere
findings.body: `className="minis-scale-popover …"` on the scale popover doesn't match anything. `rg minis-scale-popover` finds only this line: there is no rule in `global.css` and no reference in the component or e2e tests. Every other `minis-*` class added in this change has a rule in `global.css`. This one is a leftover name that suggests styling which doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Remove `minis-scale-popover` from the className.

findings.title: Summary-bar hidden assertions pass even when the CSS is broken
findings.body: The new test finds the bar's button with getByRole and no includeHidden. Once the bar gets aria-hidden="true", the locator stops matching the button, and toBeHidden counts a missing element as a pass. So the checks here and at line 328 would still pass if the bar stayed visible on screen the whole time, for example if the `.minis-summary-bar[data-visible='true']` selector in global.css were changed to `.minis-summary-bar`. The positive checks after scrolling don't catch that regression either.
findings.fix: For the negative checks, use getByRole with includeHidden: true. First assert the button is in the DOM, then assert it is hidden, so aria-hidden can't stand in for the visual state.

findings.title: Summary-bar 'Скачать PDF' gives no visible feedback: status, failure and draft-error text live only in the off-screen card
findings.body: The bar's download button calls the same `download()` as the card. All feedback for that action still renders only inside `.minis-header-pdf`, which is out of view whenever the bar is showing: the busy label ('Подготовка PDF…'), the busy status, `message` (e.g. the store's `failureMessage` set in `render()` on renderer failure) and `draftError`. Example: a user scrolled down the minis list clicks 'Скачать PDF' in the bar and rendering fails. No file arrives and the error text is never visible. The same happens when a row's count or custom-size draft is invalid: the bar's button is disabled with no visible reason. The old sidebar was sticky, so this feedback stayed on screen. The `role=status` regions are still announced to screen readers.
findings.fix: Mirror the busy label and `message`/`draftError` (or a compact form) in the summary bar, or scroll back to the card when an error appears after a bar-triggered action.

findings.title: 'Изменить' calls focus() before scrollIntoView, so the page jumps and the smooth/reduced-motion scroll mostly never runs
findings.body: `firstField?.focus()` runs without `preventScroll`. The 'Формат' trigger is off-screen at that point (the bar only shows while the header is out of view), so the browser instantly scrolls it into view. Only then does `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto' })` run, from the already-scrolled position, and it just nudges the page. The intended smooth slide back to the header never happens, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` branch has almost no effect. The end state is correct (card in view, focus on Формат, bar hidden). The e2e test only checks that final state, so it cannot catch this.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` and keep `scrollIntoView` as the only scroll.

findings.title: Summary bar's settings line is clipped with an ellipsis on narrow screens (truncate is in PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:920)
findings.body: The clipping comes from the summary span at `src/components/PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:920`, which has `truncate` (nowrap + overflow hidden + ellipsis). The CSS line cited is not the cause. `settingsSummary` (lines 484–496) can contain up to five segments, e.g. `A4 · поля 5 мм · <base style> · обрезка, нумерация · масштаб 100 мм`. That is about 70 characters, far more than fits in roughly 300 px. The `@container (width < 40rem)` rules in `src/styles/global.css` (around lines 374–384) wrap the flex row and give the span `flex: 1 1 100%`, so it gets a full line to itself. It still never wraps, though, so the trailing segments (cropping/numbering and printer scale) are hidden behind an ellipsis. The bar exists to show the current settings at a glance, and nothing in it reveals the clipped text.
findings.fix: In src/components/PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:920 or under the narrow container query in global.css, let the span wrap (e.g. `white-space: normal` on `.minis-summary-content > span` at width < 40rem, or replace `truncate` with wrapping text at narrow widths).

findings.title: Браузерный тест не проверяет закрытие окна масштаба
findings.body: Браузерный сценарий открывает окно масштаба и переводит фокус из поля, но не проверяет закрытие по Escape или внешнему клику, возврат фокуса и восстановление действий PDF после неверного значения. Поэтому регрессия этих действий в браузере оставит браузерные тесты зелёными, хотя цель изменения прямо требует, чтобы они обнаруживали такую поломку.
findings.fix: Добавить браузерные сценарии с Escape и внешним кликом, проверкой фокуса и доступности действий PDF после неверного ввода.

findings.title: Summary bar uses translucent backdrop-blur (glassmorphism), which DESIGN.md forbids
findings.body: `.minis-summary-bar` combines a 94%-opaque `color-mix(... transparent)` background, `backdrop-filter: blur(0.75rem)` and a soft `box-shadow`. That is the frosted-glass effect `docs/DESIGN.md:58` rules out ("Без градиентов, теней-стекляшек, glassmorphism"), and `docs/DESIGN.md:153` says not to use drop-shadow by default. No other style in `src/` uses `backdrop-filter`. So the one sticky surface on `/paper-minis` breaks from the paper-and-ink design system, and later tools may copy it.
findings.fix: Use an opaque `background: var(--color-surface-elevated)` with the existing `border-block-end`, and drop `backdrop-filter` and the shadow.

findings.title: Scale popover className repeats the primitive's styles, adds a border on top of its ring, and carries an unused hook class
findings.body: The new `Popover` primitive (`src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37`) already applies `rounded-lg bg-popover shadow-md ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, and `--color-popover` is `surface-elevated` (`global.css:76`). The only consumer passes `rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-elevated p-4 shadow-md` again. `twMerge` does not dedupe `border` against `ring-1`, so the popover renders with both a border and a ring. `minis-scale-popover` matches no CSS rule, test or e2e reference, so it does nothing and suggests styling that doesn't exist. This is the primitive's first consumer, so later consumers will likely copy the duplication.
findings.fix: Pass only what differs, e.g. `className="w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-2rem))] p-4"`, and drop `minis-scale-popover`. Or change the primitive to `ring-border`/`border` to match `select.tsx:63`.

findings.title: Accordion primitive has no importers left after this change, but its classes still compile into the client CSS
findings.body: `ui/accordion.tsx` was added for the Paper minis fold panel (#133), and this change removed its only import: `rg 'ui/accordion' src` finds nothing. The primitive is internal (no published package or external consumer), so it is dead code that contributors may still treat as an endorsed primitive. `global.css` uses plain `@import 'tailwindcss'` with no `@source` limits, so Tailwind v4 still scans the file and emits its utilities and the accordion keyframes into `dist/_astro/*.css`. Those bytes count against the 10 kB 'Client CSS' limit in `.size-limit.json`, and this same change adds about 190 lines of CSS. The JS is tree-shaken.
findings.fix: Delete `src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`. Keep `react-aria-components`, because the new `ui/popover.tsx` depends on it.

findings.title: The e2e 'bar hidden' assertions only check aria-hidden, not whether the CSS actually hides the bar or keeps it on screen
findings.body: The bar's button is located with `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. Playwright role locators skip `aria-hidden` subtrees by default, and the bar has `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}`. So `toBeHidden()` at lines 298 and 328 passes because the locator matches nothing, whatever the bar's CSS (`visibility: hidden` / `transform: translateY(-100%)` and the `[data-visible='true']` override) is doing. The positive `toBeVisible()` checks (311, 335) need a box and no `visibility: hidden`, but they do not check that the bar is inside the viewport. The test would still pass if: (1) the visible rule keeps `translateY(-100%)` and the bar sits above the viewport; (2) the base hide rule is lost and the fixed bar covers the top of the page while the card is in view; (3) the fixed bar is positioned against an ancestor (the `.minis-editor` `container-type`, in Safari before 18.2) and scrolls away. The goal requires the browser tests to fail when the bar's visibility breaks.
findings.fix: Locate the bar regardless of ARIA (`page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or `getByRole(..., { includeHidden: true })`). Assert `toBeInViewport()` when the card is out of view, and `not.toBeInViewport()` or `toHaveCSS('visibility', 'hidden')` when it is in view.

findings.title: Браузерный тест не проверяет закрытие popover с неверным значением
findings.body: Тест вводит допустимое значение и переводит фокус клавишей Tab, но не закрывает popover через Escape или щелчок снаружи. Поэтому он останется зелёным, если в браузере закрытие перестанет возвращать фокус или оставит неверный черновик блокировать действия PDF. Цель изменения требует, чтобы браузерные тесты обнаруживали эти регрессии; проверки в happy-dom не проверяют поведение браузера.
findings.fix: Добавить браузерные сценарии с неверным измерением: закрыть popover через Escape и щелчком снаружи, затем проверить доступность действий PDF и соответствующее возвращение фокуса.

findings.title: The bar's 'hidden' assertions only check aria-hidden; they never check that the CSS actually hides the bar
findings.body: `edit` is defined as `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. By default Playwright's role locators skip anything ARIA-hidden. The bar has `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:917). So whenever the card is in view, the locator matches nothing, and `toBeHidden()` at line 298 (before scrolling) and line 328 (after clicking Изменить) passes. That holds whatever the bar's CSS is doing. The thing that actually keeps the bar off screen is `.minis-summary-bar { transform: translateY(-100%); visibility: hidden }` together with the `[data-visible='true']` override. If those rules break while the React state is still correct (for example the default hide rule is dropped or overridden), the fixed bar stays painted at z-index 40 over the top of the page and the card, and this test still passes. The 'visible' half of the test is fine, because `toBeVisible` and the click inside the bar need the CSS to show it. What I observed: the locator, the aria-hidden toggle and the CSS rules. What I inferred: that the test stays green under that CSS regression. The goal requires that the browser tests fail if the bar's visibility breaks, and only the 'shown' direction is guarded.
findings.fix: For the hidden checks, locate the bar regardless of ARIA, e.g. `page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or `getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить', includeHidden: true })`, and assert `toBeHidden()` or `not.toBeInViewport()` on that.

findings.title: Settings summary is clipped on narrow screens and the browser test cannot detect it
findings.body: At about 320 px wide, the summary (format, margins, base style, trim, numbering, scale) does not fit on one line. `truncate` hides the end, so the user cannot see part of the current settings before downloading the PDF. The browser test runs at 1280 px and checks visibility and the full textContent, so it does not detect visual truncation.
findings.fix: Allow the summary to wrap onto multiple lines, or provide a way to see it in full.

findings.title: 'closes on Escape and an outside click' repeats the dismissal contract already owned by the test.each above it
findings.body: The `test.each` at line 104 already closes the popover by Escape and by an outside pointerdown. It then reopens it via `getByRole('button', { name: triggerName })` and reads the spinbutton again. If dismissal broke (for example `shouldCloseOnInteractOutside={() => false}`, or a missing Escape handler), the modal popover would stay open and RAC's aria-hide-outside would hide the trigger. That `getByRole` would then throw and the test.each would go red. Every edit that turns this standalone test red also turns the test.each red, so it adds no coverage and still has to be maintained.
findings.fix: Delete the standalone dismissal test, or merge its single `pointerDown`+`click` variant into the test.each cases and name the test.each as the owner of the dismissal contract.
